metadata.title: Balsm - Open Source Healthcare Platform
metadata.description: Join Balsm - the open source healthcare platform built for providers, patients, and developers. Transparent, community-driven, and accessible to all.

cloudMeta.title: Balsm Cloud — the optional cloud layer
cloudMeta.description: Sync, managed backup, and lab integration on top of Balsm — only when you choose. Arabic-first, PDPL-compliant, sovereign by design.

hero.subtitle: The optional cloud layer on top of Balsm. Your system runs entirely on its own — the cloud adds sync, backup, and lab integration, only when you decide. Your sovereignty stays yours.

adds.title: Extra power — without giving up control.

items.title: Managed backup
items.desc: Automatic encrypted snapshots — your data is safe, even if your device fails.

items.title: Lab integration
items.desc: Orders and results over FHIR — landing in the patient record directly and accurately.

items.title: Freedom to leave

map.title: From Egypt first, to the ocean and the Gulf.
map.desc: Balsm starts in Egypt first. Balsm Cloud is designed to grow with it across the Arab world — country by country, when the time is right, not before.

phase3.title: Phase 3 vision — the Cloud
phase3.desc: As Balsm Cloud expands, the Gulf states are the next destination.

longterm.title: Long-term vision
longterm.desc: From the Atlantic to the Arabian Sea — the same Balsm, when each country's time comes.

map.mapLabel: Schematic map of the Arab world: Egypt as the launch focus, the Gulf states in the Phase 3 vision, and the remaining Arab countries in the long-term vision.

invest.title: Not a product vision. A civilizational one — with a clear business model.
invest.desc: The infrastructure is open and free, so it spreads on patient demand. Revenue comes from the optional cloud layer — a network effect that's hard to displace.

homeMeta.title: Balsm — the community-owned healthcare OS
homeMeta.description: The first community-owned healthcare OS for the Arab world — Arabic-first, offline-ready, and fully open source. From Alexandria to Aswan.

hero.subtitle: The first community-owned healthcare OS in the Arab world — Arabic-first, offline-ready, and fully open source. From Alexandria to Aswan.
hero.tagline: The community-owned healthcare OS for the Arab world.

problem.title: A fragmented health system — and your data lost between its cracks.
problem.desc: The Arab patient moves between pharmacy, clinic, and lab with no single connected record. And the existing options each fail, in their own way.

cards.title: Paper and WhatsApp
cards.desc: Free and familiar — but no continuity, no security, no record that lasts. Data is lost with the first prescription.

cards.title: Legacy local systems
cards.desc: Arabic, but closed, expensive, and unable to work offline. They trap you without giving you ownership of your data.

cards.title: Foreign cloud platforms
cards.desc: Powerful, but built abroad, blind to your context, and placing Arab health data on distant servers.

how.title: One system. Three layers. A full circle of care.
how.desc: From Balsm Pro to the patient app to Balsm Cloud — each works on its own, and grows stronger together.

slices.title: Patient app
slices.desc: Your entire health journey in one place — every prescription, visit, and test. On your device, by a design that never leaves it.

slices.title: Balsm Pro app
slices.desc: For your clinic or pharmacy: dispensing, inventory, patient files, and management — fully offline, and compliant with the controlled-drugs Law 182/1960.

slices.title: Balsm Cloud
slices.desc: The optional cloud layer — cross-branch sync, backup, and lab integration. You subscribe only when you choose.

app.title: Your health, finally in its rightful place.
app.desc: Carry your complete health record in your pocket — in Arabic, on your device, going nowhere you didn't choose.
bullets: Every prescription, test, and visit on one timeline
Works offline — syncs only when you choose
Your data is yours alone — no middleman, no selling, no compromise

features.title: Everything a pharmacy and clinic need — in one system.

cards.title: Point of sale
cards.desc: Fast dispensing with item codes, Arabic receipt printing, and pricing in Egyptian pounds.

cards.title: Inventory
cards.desc: Live quantity tracking, low-stock alerts, and expiry dates before they surprise you.

cards.title: Dispensing & prescriptions
cards.desc: Link prescription to patient, a connected medication history, and drug-interaction alerts.

cards.title: Controlled drugs
cards.desc: Schedule 182/1960 register, mandatory pharmacist signature, and a full audit trail.

cards.title: Staff & permissions
cards.desc: Staff roles, fine-grained permissions, and shifts — everyone sees only what concerns them.

cards.title: Reports & insurance
cards.desc: Daily sales, profits, and insurance claims — reports you grasp at a glance.

offline.quote: “The internet will go down someday. Balsm Pro won't notice.”
offline.desc: It's built this way: a pharmacy in a village near Aswan keeps dispensing medicine even through two full days of outage. Everything local, everything working. Sync waits until you choose — not before.
